class.name: TerrainLayer
class.brief_description: A single paintable ground material inside a [Terrain3D].
class.description: [TerrainLayer] describes one ground material a [Terrain3D]'s Paint brush can blend in: an albedo texture, an optional normal map, an optional packed occlusion/roughness/metallic ([member orm_texture]) map, and how large one texture tile is in world space ([member uv_scale]). This resource is pure configuration; it does not store where it is painted. [Terrain3D] combines every layer's textures into shared [Texture2DArray]s and blends between at most two layers at a time at each point of the terrain, recorded in [TerrainData]'s control map (see [method Terrain3D.paint_layer]). Layer textures are resampled to a common size when built into those arrays, so very high-resolution source textures do not need to match each other exactly.

members.member: The base color texture for this layer. Until this is set, the layer renders as flat gray.
A display name for this layer, shown in [Terrain3D]'s Paint brush layer list.
An optional tangent-space normal map for this layer. If unset, the layer uses a flat normal (no extra surface detail beyond the terrain's own geometry).

An optional packed occlusion (red channel), roughness (green channel), and metallic (blue channel) texture for this layer, matching the convention used elsewhere in Godot (see [member BaseMaterial3D.orm_texture]). If unset, the layer uses full occlusion, medium roughness, and no metallic.
The size, in meters, that one tile of this layer's textures covers on the terrain. Smaller values tile the texture more densely (a smaller, more repeated pattern); larger values stretch it further.
